idea: Laundry pickup and drop for students in my university hostels

strategist.problem: Hostel student at 11pm realizes they have no clean clothes for an 8am class or placement interview, and the nearest dhobi won't collect or return laundry on their schedule.
strategist.target_customer: Hostel residents at a mid-size Indian university paying ₹5,000-₹15,000 monthly, too busy with classes and fests to wash clothes themselves and willing to pay to never think about laundry.
strategist.mission: Pick up, wash and deliver hostel students' laundry on a fixed weekly schedule so they never run out of clean clothes during term.

competitors.name: Local dhobi/washerman near campus
competitors.differentiator: We give fixed pickup-delivery slots, per-kg pricing shown upfront and WhatsApp tracking instead of drop-off queues and cash haggling.

competitors.name: Hostel washing machines and common bathrooms
competitors.differentiator: We save 3-4 hours a week of washing, drying and folding in shared, often crowded or broken machines.

competitors.name: Urban Company / local laundry apps in the city
competitors.differentiator: We only serve this campus, so pickup is same-day within hostel blocks and there's no app download or surge pricing.

scope_cuts: No custom mobile app — a WhatsApp number and a Google Form for pickup requests cover the first 50 customers.
No dry-cleaning, ironing-only or bulk institutional contracts — only wash-and-fold per kg for hostel students until one route is profitable.
No hiring delivery staff — founder and one batchmate run pickup and drop on bicycles for the first term.

stack.name: WhatsApp Business
stack.why: Primary channel for pickup requests, slot confirmation, and delivery updates via quick replies and catalogue.

stack.name: Google Forms
stack.why: Collects pickup address, kg estimate, and UPI payment link without building a custom app.

stack.name: Razorpay
stack.why: Generates UPI payment links for per-kg billing and monthly plans directly in WhatsApp.

stack.name: Notion
stack.why: Tracks daily pickup routes, kg weights, and payment status for the founder and batchmate.

stack.name: Canva
stack.why: Creates WhatsApp status posters and hostel notice board flyers for fixed weekly slots.

ai_tools.name: ChatGPT
ai_tools.why: Drafts WhatsApp quick replies, pricing explanations, and handles student queries instantly.

ai_tools.name: Claude
ai_tools.why: Writes the one-page service description and generates Canva-ready text for promotional posts.

mvp_features: Per-kg wash-and-fold service with same-day pickup and next-day delivery for hostel blocks.
Monthly unlimited laundry plan with fixed weekly pickup and drop slots for 5 kg per week.
WhatsApp-based order tracking with automated payment link generation for every pickup request.

tool_costs.price_note: 2% + GST per payment, no setup fee or AMC. Price checked 2026-11-02 on https://razorpay.com/pricing/

first_10_steps: Set up a WhatsApp Business account with a catalogue listing per-kg rates and monthly plan details.
Create a Google Form for pickup requests that includes address, kg estimate, and a Razorpay payment link field.
Generate 5 UPI payment links in Razorpay for common kg ranges (2kg, 5kg, 10kg) to share via WhatsApp.
Draft 3 WhatsApp quick replies for order confirmation, pickup time, and delivery status using ChatGPT.
Design a 2-page Canva flyer showing the weekly pickup schedule and pricing for hostel notice boards.
Recruit one batchmate to help with pickup and drop on bicycles for the first two weeks.
Post the flyer and service details in 3 hostel WhatsApp groups and 2 class groups with a 20% discount for the first 10 orders.
Collect the first 10 laundry pickups, weigh the clothes, and send the exact payment link via WhatsApp.
Track all pickups, weights, and payments in a Notion database to calculate the actual cost per kg.
Review the first week's data to adjust the per-kg price and confirm the most popular pickup time slot.

pricing.name: Per-kg wash and fold
features: ₹50 per kg, minimum 3 kg per pickup (₹150 minimum order)
Same-day pickup, next-day delivery in hostel blocks
WhatsApp tracking and UPI payment link

pricing.name: Monthly 5kg plan
features: 5 kg every week, fixed pickup slot
Covers a full month of hostel laundry

pricing.name: Monthly 10kg plan
features: 10 kg every week for heavy users

revenue_targets.notes: First 10 orders at 20% discount; mostly per-kg users at ₹50/kg with 3kg minimum from 3 hostel groups.
3 monthly plan subscribers plus 9 per-kg users; batchmate on second bicycle route.
8 monthly plan subscribers plus 17 per-kg users; one route profitable, second route started.

key_assumptions: Hostel students will pay ₹50/kg with a 3kg minimum because the nearest dhobi charges ₹30-₹50/kg with no fixed slot (assumption, unverified).
delivery_cost_per_customer of ₹340 = ₹180 goods/route labour share + ₹160 for 2 hours of founder+batchmate time at ₹80/hour, to be validated against minute-logged times from the first 10 pickups.
Average paying customer pays ₹850/month blended across tiers, giving ₹510 gross margin per customer after delivery cost.
Founder puts in ₹15,000 of savings; no external funding.

channels.name: Hostel WhatsApp Groups
channels.tactic: Post a 150-word service description with a 20% discount code for the first 10 orders in 5 specific hostel resident groups (2 per block) and 2 class groups, then DM every person who replies 'interested' within 2 hours to schedule a pickup.

channels.name: Physical Notice Boards
channels.tactic: Print 50 A5 flyers on Canva (₹50 ink/paper) and pin them on the notice boards of 4 hostel messes and 2 common rooms, including a QR code to the Google Form and a 'First 10 get 20% off' offer.

first_10_customers: Walk to the 3 nearest hostel blocks and ask the warden or senior for permission to pin flyers on the notice board and share the service in the block WhatsApp group.
DM 20 batchmates and 10 juniors in class groups with the cold message, offering a free 2kg wash-and-fold pilot to the first 3 who reply.
Set up a WhatsApp Business catalogue with the per-kg rate and monthly plan, and share the catalogue link in the 5 hostel groups with the discount code.
Personally pick up the first 5 laundry loads from the mess area at 10am, wash them at the local dhobi (negotiate a bulk rate for 10kg+), and deliver them back by 6pm the next day.
Send a WhatsApp status update with photos of the folded clothes in bags to all 50 contacts in the hostel groups to show proof of delivery.
Ask the first 3 pilot users for a 1-line testimonial and share it in the hostel groups to convert the remaining 7 paying customers.
growth.cold_message:
Hey, I noticed you're in [Hostel Name] and probably hate washing clothes in the common bathroom.
I'm a student here too, and I'm offering same-day laundry pickup and next-day delivery for ₹40/kg, with a 20% discount for the first 10 orders.
Want me to pick up your laundry tomorrow at 10am? Just reply with your room number and I'll send the UPI link.

objections.objection: I don't trust you with my clothes; what if you lose them or damage them?
objections.response: I'm a student in the same hostel, so I can't afford to lose your trust. I'll give you a free 2kg pilot wash first—if you're happy with the quality and timing, you can pay for the next pickup. I'll also send photos of your folded clothes before I deliver them.

objections.objection: The local dhobi is cheaper and I already use them.
objections.response: The dhobi charges ₹30-₹50/kg but you have to drop off and pick up yourself, which takes 30-45 minutes each way. I pick up from your room at 10am and deliver by 6pm the next day, so you save 1-2 hours a week. Plus, my pricing is fixed at ₹40/kg with no haggling, and you get a WhatsApp tracking link for every pickup.

critic.verdict: The plan is a credible campus-first laundry service with realistic pricing, free tooling and a founder-sized workload. It stays faithful to the pickup-and-drop idea and fits the bootstrapped student constraints well. Main gaps are around delivery cost realism and the growth playbook's reliance on unproven dhobi outsourcing.
critic.biggest_risk: The founder has no proven laundry partner or own washing setup, so the first pickups depend on negotiating an untested bulk rate with a local dhobi — if that rate or turnaround fails, delivery cost and next-day promise both collapse before the first 10 customers.
